Abdelahee faced six counts of attempted first-degree murder, seven counts of aggravated discharge, of a firearm, an aggravated battery. According to local reporting, investigators, quickly discovered that Abdullahi chose his victim because of his Jewish faith, leading prosecutors to formally charge him with hate crimes and terrorism. On November 22, 2024, Abdullahi appeared in court for the first time, where prosecutors revealed that, in the days prior to the attack, Abdelahee saved the locations of nearby synagogues, searched for Jewish Community Center, and searched for a gun store. His phone also included more than 100 anti-Semitic and pro-Hamas images and videos. According to the Chicago Sun Times, Abdullahi's public defender stated in court that he was an immigrant from Mauritania, who lived in the United States for two years, and worked at an Amazon warehouse, making this case the only known instance of an immigrant crossing the U.S. border illegally to commit a terrorist attack. Eight days later, Cook County Sheriff's staff were conducting routine security checks at CIRMAC health services and found Abdullahi unresponsive in his cell. He was taken to Mount Sinai Hospital where he was pronounced dead. The Cook County Medical Examiner's Office ruled Abdelahee's death as suicide. His victim was released from the hospital five days after the shooting, however, additional information regarding his condition could not be obtained.
